fields.value: Porcelain Veneers in Fortitude Valley

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: If you have teeth that are discoloured, chipped, uneven or slightly misshapen, porcelain veneers may help you feel more comfortable with your smile. At Precision Dental, we take a careful, conservative approach to veneers, beginning with a detailed conversation about what you would like to change and whether veneers are the most suitable option for you.

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Veneers are a significant decision, and they are not right for everyone. Our role is to give you clear, balanced information so you can decide with confidence.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Are Porcelain Veneers?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Porcelain veneers are thin, custom-made shells of dental ceramic that are bonded to the front surfaces of teeth. They can change the colour, shape, length and proportions of the teeth they cover. Porcelain resists staining well and reflects light in a similar way to natural enamel.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: To create space for a veneer, a thin layer of enamel is usually removed from the front of the tooth. Because this change is permanent, the tooth will always need a veneer or another restoration to protect it in future. Veneers can chip or wear over time and may eventually need replacement.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Are Porcelain Veneers Right for You?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Porcelain veneers may be considered for adults with:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Teeth that are stained or discoloured and do not respond well to whitening

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Chipped, worn or irregularly shaped teeth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Small gaps between the front teeth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Teeth that appear too short or uneven in length

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Mild alignment concerns, where orthodontic treatment is not preferred

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Veneers are generally best suited to people with healthy teeth and gums. If you have active decay or gum disease, we will treat these first. If you grind or clench your teeth, we will discuss how this may affect veneers and whether a protective night splint is needed. For some patients, teeth whitening, composite resin veneers or Invisalign may be a more conservative alternative.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Consultation and Planning

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Your journey begins with a comprehensive examination, digital X-rays and photographs. We check your gum health and bite, then listen closely to what you would like to change. Where appropriate, we use Digital Smile Design to help you visualise the proposed changes before any treatment begins.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Preparation

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: At your preparation appointment, local anaesthetic is used to keep you comfortable. A thin layer of enamel is gently removed, and a digital scan of your teeth is taken. Temporary veneers may be placed while your final veneers are made.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Fitting

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Once your veneers are ready, we check their fit, shape and shade with you. When you are happy, each veneer is bonded securely to the tooth, and your bite is carefully adjusted.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Look after your veneers as you would your natural teeth. Brush twice daily with a soft toothbrush, floss or use interdental brushes each day, and attend regular check-ups and cleans. Avoid biting directly on very hard objects such as ice, pens or fingernails. If you play contact sport, wear a custom mouthguard, and if you grind your teeth, a night splint can help protect your veneers. Some sensitivity is common for a short time after treatment.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for Porcelain Veneers

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for Porcelain Veneers

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Dr Billy Choi has more than two decades of experience in general and cosmetic dentistry. We take time to understand your goals, use digital planning to support precise results, and always discuss the benefits, limitations and alternatives of veneers. You will never feel rushed into a decision.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Interest-free payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How long do porcelain veneers last?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The lifespan of veneers varies from person to person. It depends on factors such as oral hygiene, grinding habits and regular maintenance. Veneers may chip, wear or need replacement over time, and we will discuss this with you at your consultation.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Is the veneer process uncomfortable?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Local anaesthetic is used during preparation to keep you comfortable. Some patients notice mild sensitivity or tenderness for a few days after treatment, which usually settles on its own.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will my veneers look natural?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We carefully select the shade, shape and translucency of your veneers to complement your face and surrounding teeth. You will be able to review their appearance before they are bonded.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can veneers be removed?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Because a thin layer of enamel is usually removed, porcelain veneers are considered permanent. If a veneer is damaged or removed, the tooth will need a new veneer or another restoration.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: What is the difference between porcelain and composite veneers?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Porcelain veneers are made in ceramic and are generally more resistant to staining. Composite veneers are shaped directly onto the teeth, usually need less preparation and are easier to repair, but may stain or chip more readily.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I whiten my teeth after getting veneers?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Whitening does not change the colour of porcelain. If you are considering whitening, it is best done before your veneers are made, so your veneers can be matched to your new shade.
